value.textContent:
Hey folks 

 We’re about a month into the spaces alpha! From what I can tell, it’s going along pretty nicely. We pushed out one breaking change about two weeks back, but it’s been pretty stable apart from that.

 I wanted to share a list of some of the open questions we’re still noodling on. Many of these will likely involve breaking changes. Most of these are not truly “open”, we have opinions on them and need to just nail it down. However, if anything is important to you, please share your thoughts.

 We’re hoping to hit all of these (and any other changes of similar scope) by end of October.

 Any change we make will first be made as a PR on the proposal repo . Then it will be merged when the implementation is updated and deployed. This happens on Thursdays and will be recorded in the alpha updates Discourse thread .

 If you missed it, we’ll be doing an office hours session on Thursday (sept 24) to chat about the alpha, answer questions, and collect feedback.

 Open write spaces

 Should the PDS offer spaces that anyone can write to?

 Proposal merged: 0016 Atproto spaces: simplespace write access by dholms · Pull Request #105 · bluesky-social/proposals · GitHub 

 Space credential expiration/revocation

 Do we need a revocation path?

 Should expiration be shorter than 2 hrs?

 Current proposal: 0016: Shorten expiration time and add revocation method by dholms · Pull Request #109 · bluesky-social/proposals · GitHub 

 Public spaces

 Are public spaces in any way different from permissioned spaces?

 Should space authorities be able to mint a credential when no delegation token is offered (ie unauthenticated)?

 Of course this is always “possible”, but is it considered “offspec”?

 Could/should public space repos be rebroadcastable (ie signed)?

 DID docs

 Do we definitely want new service/key identifiers?

 What exactly are the semantics?

 For instance, can space authority sign a space credential with their #atproto key (specified through kid claim) if they also have an #atproto_space key in their DID document?

 Repo serialization

 The currently-specced serialization format sucks.

 Should this be a CAR file? Or should it be a new format? (for instance STAR-lite )

 Do we need a “multi-repo” format used in account migration?

 DPoP

 Is this the right fit in the credential flow?

 Technically specified for OAuth.

 We could have our own construction using HTTP signatures or similar

 getSpaceCredential

 Can you use other types of proofs besides delegation token & client attestation?

 re: 0016 make getSpaceCredential more generic? · Issue #97 · bluesky-social/proposals · GitHub 

 Commits and signatures

 Should signatures be on the commit or should they be transferred as metadata (ie in HTTP headers)?

 Should we offer a deniable signature on single-record requests? (ie via com.atproto.space.getRecord )

 I think Bryan convinced me that the HMAC signing scheme needs a consumer-provided nonce. Expect some sort of tweak here

 Account status

 What is the account status of a space authority?

 Is it the same as normal account status? Can #atproto_pds and #atproto_space_host vary?

 Sync scaling/reliability

 Can we make write notifications less lossy?

 Does PDS (space repo) need to remember and retry notifications to space host?

 Does space host need to provide better self-healing mechanisms?

 Space deletion

 Is the deletion flow robust enough? It is lossy & best-effort.

 Do members need to receive a notification of space deletion? Or does just syncers suffice, and applications re in charge of informing members?

 URI scheme

 Should we try to resolve IETF syntax issue for space URIs (ie dropping slashes, ie just at: )

 Should we support either blobs or versioned records in space URIs (things we’ve wanted in public URIs but just haven’t gotten around to)?

Thank you for laying out the questions for the post-alpha phase. I look forward to Spaces becoming a foundation for a wide range of apps. I support a design that provides shared mechanisms for authorization and sync while leaving apps and Space authorities to decide the policies appropriate to their use cases.

 Below are my comments from an app implementation and operations perspective, including points I support, concrete use cases, and behavior I would like to clarify.

 Open write spaces

 I support open write spaces. They would be useful for receiving information, such as membership requests or inquiries, from people who have not already been registered as members. Independent read and write settings are particularly useful here: being able to submit something should not imply being able to read other people’s submissions.

 Space credential expiration/revocation

 I support shorter credential lifetimes combined with an explicit revocation mechanism. Using short lifetimes as the baseline, with revocation of individual credentials when access needs to be withdrawn sooner, seems like a good way to make revocation take effect promptly without requiring a call to the authority on every read.

 Public spaces

 For public spaces, I think the specification should allow a Space authority to issue read credentials without a delegation token. It seems natural that an app should not need to maintain someone’s user session just to retrieve public information. I support keeping the same data structures and sync APIs for public and private spaces while allowing the conditions for issuing credentials to differ.

 I also support signatures that remain verifiable after redistribution, so that data from public spaces can be authenticated when retrieved from mirrors or archives.

 DID docs

 I support dedicated service and key identifiers for Spaces. The option to continue using #atproto_pds and #atproto also seems useful for migration from existing services.

 Allowing Space Credentials to be signed with #atproto even when a dedicated key is present should be an option for compatibility, rather than a requirement for every Space authority.

 Repo serialization

 For serializing a single repo, I would prefer CAR if it meets the requirements, since it allows reuse of existing libraries and tools. I am also interested in formats such as STAR-lite, but I think the choice should be based on how much they improve transfer size, memory usage, and implementation complexity for the data structures used by Spaces.

 A format that bundles multiple repos would be useful for account migration and backups. Reusing the serialization format for individual repos within that bundle would make it easier to share implementation between routine sync and migration.

 DPoP

 I support continuing to use DPoP. When the same Space Credential is presented to multiple repo hosts, binding it to the presenter’s key seems appropriate to prevent a host that receives the credential from reusing it to access another host.

 There is also value in reusing implementations and experience from AT Protocol’s use of OAuth. As long as its application to Spaces can be clearly specified, I do not think the fact that DPoP was defined for OAuth is, by itself, a reason to choose a different mechanism.

 getSpaceCredential

 I support allowing getSpaceCredential to work with authorization methods that do not require a user’s delegation token. For example, a backup or search indexing service explicitly authorized by a Space administrator should not need to keep maintaining and refreshing a particular user’s OAuth session for ongoing sync.

 It would be useful to establish the service’s identity through client attestation and issue a Space Credential based on explicit permission granted to that service by the Space authority. This would allow access for services to be managed independently of individual user sessions, while repo hosts continue to use the same Space Credential verification mechanism.

 Commits and signatures

 I support providing deniable signatures for individual record fetches as well. For example, a client displaying just one linked post, or a tool fetching only the records it needs, would benefit from being able to verify those records without syncing the entire repo.

 For permissioned data, it would be good for these partial fetches to preserve deniability in the same way as regular repo sync.

 Account status

 If #atproto_pds and #atproto_space_host can be operated as separate services, I support treating their account statuses independently as well. For example, someone might deactivate their PDS account for public posts while continuing to act as the authority for a community Space hosted by a separate service.

 Deactivating an account on one service should not necessarily imply deactivating it on another service associated with the same DID. I think the design should distinguish the availability of an author’s records from their active status as a Space authority.

 Sync scaling/reliability

 It would be good to have a mechanism for retrying write notifications from repo hosts to Space hosts after an outage. I am particularly concerned about a new writer’s first notification being lost, with no subsequent writes. If the Space host does not know about that writer, wouldn’t the writer remain undiscoverable even if a syncer periodically checks listRepos ?

 I would like a guarantee that the writer can be discovered and synced in this case without requiring another write. If notifications can be coalesced to the latest revision of each repo, there should be no need to retain and resend every write notification individually.

 Space deletion

 I support sending Space deletion notifications to syncers and leaving member notifications to apps. How users should be notified depends on the use case, and I do not think the Spaces protocol needs to require enumerating all readers or managing their notification destinations for this purpose.

 I also support using SpaceDeleted during credential renewal to detect deletion when a notification has been missed. Distinguishing deletion from a temporary failure would let syncers proceed with deleting their local copies and derived data without depending solely on receiving a notification.

 URI scheme

 I support adopting a format that conforms to standard URI syntax, provided that Spaces will not end up using a mixture of the existing AT URI format and the new URI format. I see value in integration with existing link handling, such as treating references in documents as links in native apps and opening them in an app that handles the scheme.

 I also support being able to reference a blob or a specific version of a record with a single URI. This would be useful for linking to attachments and making it explicit which version of a document or post is being cited.

dholms.xyz: 

 Sync scaling/reliability

 Can we make write notifications less lossy?

 Does PDS (space repo) need to remember and retry notifications to space host?

 Does space host need to provide better self-healing mechanisms?

 I was about to make a separate topic but noticed this was here and this is niche-ish sync concern.

 Just had a longer talk on the atproto touchers discord about recovering from situations where an appview looses it’s list of spaces it has access to for whatever reason. A bit upside of public atproto data is that, assuming your app is properly designed, you can more or less nuke your appview DB and fully or mostly fully recover your whole app just from backfill. Spaces are harder in this regard though since even the existence of a space is potentially permissioned knowledge. So if you end up “forgetting” you have access to a space you might never know when trying to backfill. For that use case it would probably be nice for space hosts to expose a “hey there space host do you have any spaces for me?” endpoint. An authenticated endpoint that services (or any identity really) can make calls to to get a list of all spaces that that space host is willing to offer that identity access to to some degree. Could be styled as a spaces version of listReposByCollection . This could feasibly also be part of space-management implementations instead of the core spaces protocol. But I think it’s worth having a generic option. Or at the very least not leaving simplespace out of it if we do decide this should be a space-management thing not a core protocol thing.

 Other stuff here I have an opinion on:

 dholms.xyz: 

 DID docs

 Do we definitely want new service/key identifiers?

 What exactly are the semantics?

 For instance, can space authority sign a space credential with their #atproto key (specified through kid claim) if they also have an #atproto_space key in their DID document?

 and

 dholms.xyz: 

 Account status

 What is the account status of a space authority?

 Is it the same as normal account status? Can #atproto_pds and #atproto_space_host vary?

 I think we definetly want space hosts to have dedicated service and key entries. I don’t have a strong opinion on the currently proposed fallback behaviour, though I might argue that not having a fallback is simpler conceptually. Similarly allowing use of an arbitrary key entry with the kid claim follows the now established pattern of how atproto JWTs work so I’d argue it’s good to keep that going. For ease of use, implementation and understanding by everyone.

 Most importantly I think that having a connected space host should not constitute that identity having an account. That resolves the account status question: space authorities have no account status unless they also have an account at a PDS, and if they do then it follows the same semantics as for all other identities with accounts. Space authorities are a lot more similar to service identities than user identities and we should treat them more as such in my opinion.

 dholms.xyz: 

 Commits and signatures

 Should signatures be on the commit or should they be transferred as metadata (ie in HTTP headers)?

 Should we offer a deniable signature on single-record requests? (ie via com.atproto.space.getRecord )

 I think Bryan convinced me that the HMAC signing scheme needs a consumer-provided nonce. Expect some sort of tweak here

 I think signature should be in the commit. Mainly makes the commit object self contained but also makes it better suited for potential future transports (or apps choosing specific custom transports).

 Single-record deniable signature would be really good if you ask me.

 dholms.xyz: 

 Public spaces

 Are public spaces in any way different from permissioned spaces?

 Should space authorities be able to mint a credential when no delegation token is offered (ie unauthenticated)?

 Of course this is always “possible”, but is it considered “offspec”?

 Could/should public space repos be rebroadcastable (ie signed)?

 I’d say public spaces are absolutely different enough to be worth considering special protocol support for. To me public spaces probably exist in two forms: spaces that have always been public and permissioned spaces that turned public. Both of these would benefit from public space commits being rebroadcastable and maybe even being allowed in the firehose/ subscribeRepos semantics. I remember talking about public spaces with @zicklag.dev a whiiiiile back and we kept returning to how loosing out on the firehose is a big big downside to private data that later got made public, but also that permissioned repos later going public is a practically unavoidable usage pattern for many app modalities. I think the sync patterns change enough in these cases that seamlessly integrating with the firehose or something similar is absolutely worth it if you ask me. For the same reasons that not using MSTs and the other existing sync primitives is worth it for permissioned spaces. Not to say it should necessarily be exactly the same primitives as existing public data, but something close to it probably.

There is a bunch here!

 An authenticated endpoint that services (or any identity really) can make calls to to get a list of all spaces that that space host is willing to offer that identity access to to some degree. Could be styled as a spaces version of listReposByCollection.

 I understand the desire for something like this, but there are a few issues with it.

 In the current design, space access is gated primarily by identity of an individual account, and then optionally by app client identity. This means that apps only get access to spaces through an active user session, like an OAuth session. If all app state has been lost, then all those sessions are gone, and the app can’t get access even if they knew to ask.

 A counter-point is that an app service does register as a syncer, and gets notifyWrite pings when any space repo in the space is updated. But that doesn’t include the actual content, and the syncing services needs to authenticate (with a space credential, from a user session) to get the actual data.

 For some applications I think this might be fine. The recovering app will gradually reindex as users log back in and grant access to their space repos, and the app backfills the entire space from the space host. If a user doesn’t re-authenticate, maybe it is good that the service can’t re-index the data?

 I’m not entirely sure how spaces that a user only has read-only access to would be discovered for indexing by the app service. Maybe this becomes modality-specific?

 One thing you can do is backfill all the discoverable “public” spaces (which have declaration records, and will hand out space credentials to anybody).

 On DID document entries:

 I was actually just thinking the opposite today: that we might be able to assume that the space host is always the account host. For individual accounts on a regular PDS with only simplespace , this will be true. And with the “group host” concept, it will also be true for group/community accounts.

 But need to think it through further.

 Public spaces:

 I kind of think it should be possible to tell if a space is re-broadcastable or not should be a permanent status, and indicated in the URI (!).

 A hard direction in particular is a space having been publicly re-broadcast, and then flipped back to non-public.

Some short updates on design progress ( @dholms.xyz can you turn the original post in to a “wiki post”? I think that is just a config flag):

 Public spaces: pretty confident we aren’t going to make any big changes here. No re-distributable cryptographic commitments, no space data on firehoses, repo hosts require space credentials for all space repos (even if “public”). As a small change, will probably update space credential endpoint so that both delegation token and client attestation are optional: that makes it clearer how to fetch “public” spaces w/o an atproto account (if the space authority allows it).

 Repo serialization: expect to ship with STAR files not CAR files

 DPoP: switched to HTTP Message Signatures last week

 Sync scaling/reliability: changes shipped last week

 Cryptographic commitment: think we might need to do proper Diffie-Helman (then KEM for post-quantum). That would mean publishing an addition key in all DID documents but not the end of the world. Also want to iterate on which fields end up in the repo commit metadata object, and which end up as an HTTP header.

 URI scheme: still furiously debating 

 Simplespace configuration: have a thread going over here: Updateable space policy by matthieusieben · Pull Request #119 · bluesky-social/proposals · GitHub , probably should have been a forum thread instead

 Have not started on a couple of the other questions yet. But generally making progress and feels to me like we are on-track to have most of these resolved by end of October, and to be able to ship some time in November.
Yes have made it wiki editable. OP author should be able to do this too FYI.

bnewbold.net: 

 A counter-point is that an app service does register as a syncer

 I was thinking mainly in terms of syncers yes. And services that may have been given long term access directly without access through a user since I expect that will become a somewhat wide spread pattern. But I can also equally see the argument that services will rediscover the spaces they need to know as time goes on and people keep using their clients. Maybe it’s even arguably better if they can’t rediscover without a user in the loop.

 bnewbold.net: 

 I was actually just thinking the opposite today: that we might be able to assume that the space host is always the account host. For individual accounts on a regular PDS with only simplespace , this will be true. And with the “group host” concept, it will also be true for group/community accounts.

 That’s probably fair. The main worry I’d have there is that you might not want to always use simplespace for those cases. But the flip side there is that you can just as well use a custom PDS implementation that implements another space management system.

 My main gripe is I don’t think that we should enforce at a protocol level that a space authority have an account. At least we shouldn’t do that if we continue to make a distinction between space hosts and PDSs, which I think is a worthwhile distinction to make. Lots of space authorities might not need an account. Forcing them to have one when they don’t need it seems a little silly to me.

value.title: A shared lexicon for *video notes*? Looking for input before I build
value.description: I’m considering tobuild an app for recording short screen videos and sharing them as video notes. Basically Loom for AT. I’d love your input on the lexicon shape before I settle it. The use case You record your screen (a window, a region or the whole display) with your voice and an optional webcam bubble, and share it as a quick explanation, similar to post-it notes or voice memos. I see two main user groups: people working together who might send each other video notes (a bug walkthrough, design feedback, a project handover), and educator creators sharing clips with their audience (tutorials, top tips…). Why a separate lexicon? These are informal notes, quick to make, and often disposable. They should not appear in the Bluesky video tab, in Bluescreen, or in any other app built for “finished” videos. Promoting a video note to a bsky (or wherever) post is of course possible, but it’s a separate explicit action. Visibility Public or unlisted first, private later. Unlisted only means the user’s profile does not list it, because ofc repo data is public. Real private notes will need Spaces. I’d like the record to survive a move into a spaces when that launches. Proposed lexicon ( {ns} is a placeholder until there is a name) Core (belonging to this app’s domain) {ns}.note : the note itself. Might include Title, description, video blob (MP4), thumbnail blob, aspect ratio, duration, capture kind (display, window, region), “listed” flag, timestamps. I like the idea of this maybe being spaced alongside other types of community lexicons for notes (text, voice, image…) {ns}.note.defs : any shared definitions such as capture kind and visibility. {ns}.comment : a comment on a note, with an optional time anchor in milliseconds and an optional parent for replies. I see bsky posts possibly used here in conjunction but not sure of the implications. {ns}.transcript : captions and transcripts, language plus a WebVTT blob, human or automatic. {ns}.collection : an ordered set of notes (e.g. for a series, project or course) Borrrorws - existing lexicons I’d reuse / connect to interactions: Streamplace streams and VODs as source material (similar to how you can create clips from youtube VODs and streams…) Bluesky posts as comments Scope My MVP scope looks something like this right now: {ns}.note as one record, carrying its own metadata, plus profile reuse and the listed flag. A desktop recorder (Electon), MP4 up to 10 minutes at 720p, uploaded straight to the user’s PDS, within its blob limit. Designed for but not built: visibility levels and Spaces, comments, transcripts, collections… Out of scope for now: Import Streamplace clips, Post to Bluesky, Bluesky posts as comments. What I’d like input on One record or more? A neutral community namespace, or an app-level namespace? A listed flag now and a visibility enum later: will that survive a move into Spaces? Is anyone else already modelling something like this, so we can share / collab? — Also, different but related to

 Why a separate lexicon? 

 These are informal notes, quick to make, and often disposable. They should not appear in the Bluesky video tab, in Bluescreen, or in any other app built for “finished” videos. Promoting a video note to a bsky (or wherever) post is of course possible, but it’s a separate explicit action.

 Visibility 

 Public or unlisted first, private later. Unlisted only means the user’s profile does not list it, because ofc repo data is public. Real private notes will need Spaces. I’d like the record to survive a move into a spaces when that launches.

 Proposed lexicon 

 ( {ns} is a placeholder until there is a name)

 Core (belonging to this app’s domain)

 {ns}.note : the note itself. Might include Title, description, video blob (MP4), thumbnail blob, aspect ratio, duration, capture kind (display, window, region), “listed” flag, timestamps. I like the idea of this maybe being spaced alongside other types of community lexicons for notes (text, voice, image…)

 Suggestions welcome across the board!

 Thanks y’all.

Great write up. I’d start with planning for spaces day 1, but you don’t really need to design anything into the lexicon for this I don’t think. That’s an app view / app concern.

 Public vs Unlisted still makes sense too, these are pretty standard patterns.

 I actually don’t think you need a limit? This is another meta item where blob size limits and other parts of the system are going to affect this.

 I probably wouldn’t put collections directly in this lexicon. We don’t have generic collections and it’s a good point: what IS a list of lexicon objects? (That’s not a feed). I guess Semble collections and Grain albums are counter examples.

 Tags are also likely to be useful.

 Comments using rich text and just holding a Bsky post embed could be a thing. And, an app can look for back links without being a comment per se. I think having a first class comment for timeline remarks is good. I’d look at what Leaflet is doing.

 I’m actually a bit confused by just seeing “note” - but I guess you’re leaning on the NS for that. I searched a couple of .video domains and there a bunch that might be relevant.

 I get what you’re thinking about “maybe it’s all notes but they are typed” … but at that point I just want a collection that can hold many different lexicons.

 For Streamplace VODs, I believe it goes beyond blobs to point at external S3 compatible storage - I don’t know how to model this, a blob OR an external link? @iame.li will tell us.

 Other than being adamant that these are “simple” video notes and not important video notes — is there anything here that doesn’t make sense for videos generally? Or is your Loom use case just a way to build an opinionated app that focuses on that style of video?

Hi – I’m working on a transcript format for atproto with Streamplace and Ionosphere, provisionally called TAML (Transcript And Media Layer). You’ve put {ns}.transcript aside for now, so it might be worth a look. Transcripts apply to any video, so one shared lexicon would save each app making its own.

 The text and word timings go in chunk records. A transcript record holds the language and speakers, says how the transcript was made, human or automatic, and points at the video record. WebVTT is generated from the records when a player needs it. For a 10-minute note that’s one transcript record and one chunk. Word timings let you show an interactive transcript or karaoke captions perhaps .

 Corrections and translations are there if you want them later – a correction is a new version, and a translation points back at the version it came from – but you don’t need them to start.

 On Boris’s point about blobs and external storage – the transcript points at the video record, so it doesn’t matter where the video bytes live.

 On comments with a time anchor – if we both count milliseconds from the start of the media, a comment could also point at a range of the transcript text.

 Spec: Transcripts on atproto and MUXL – draft recommendation · GitHub 

Guide: TAML – A Developer's Guide · GitHub 

 The record names are placeholders for now. Happy to talk it through.

value.title: Detecting spaces support
value.description: I’ve been working on a system in HappyView to automatically migrate a user’s spaces data from HappyView to their PDS if I can detect that their PDS supports spaces. It’s really hard. describeServer is the first place I checked, but it hasn’t changed in the alpha to indicate support for spaces. The DID document entries for spaces are optional with fallbacks, so we can check for them but their absence doesn’t prove anything. My current solution This is what I’ve landed on so far, but I’m looking for feedback. Right now, detection is two tiers. First, I check community.lexicon.service.describe . If the server answers it, I treat the method list as authoritative. The presence of spaces XRPCs is a definitive indicator that spaces are supported by the PDS. The second tier is required because the reference alpha PDS doesn’t implement community.lexicon.service.describe . Since it’s by far the most common PDS implementation and, thus, the primary target, I fall back to some unreliable status code-based detection: Request What the reference PDS says community.lexicon.service.describe 400 , not implemented, and notably not a 404 com.atproto.space.listSpaces with no auth 401 AuthMissing , route present com.atproto.space.<nonexistent> 400 InvalidRequest , route absent com.atproto.simplespace.getSpace with no auth 400 , route present, rejecting missing params A missing route and a present-but-unparameterised route both return 400 , but an auth-gated method returns 401 . The logic is: If we receive the same status code for everything (say all 4 requests return 405 ), we can’t reliably determine spaces support so we assume it isn’t there. If we get the expected status codes from each route, we can be reasonably confident that 1) this is a reference PDS, and 2) it has spaces support. It’s still a problem This method is, to say the least, unreliable. Somebody could be running the reference PDS between a reverse proxy that converts all error responses to 418 just for the memes, meaning the it may support spaces but HV would assume it doesn’t. A non-reference PDS may return the same status codes but have a broken implementation. It’s a minefield. Since my survey of the ecosystem shows that it’s safe for now , I’m shipping this detection system today, but I’m hoping there’s a better way. IMHO the ideal would be for the ref PDS to implement community.lexicon.service.describe . Thoughts?

 What the reference PDS says 

 community.lexicon.service.describe 
 400 , not implemented, and notably not a 404

 com.atproto.space.<nonexistent> 
 400 InvalidRequest , route absent 

 com.atproto.simplespace.getSpace with no auth 
 400 , route present, rejecting missing params

 If we receive the same status code for everything (say all 4 requests return 405 ), we can’t reliably determine spaces support so we assume it isn’t there.

 It’s still a problem

 This method is, to say the least, unreliable. Somebody could be running the reference PDS between a reverse proxy that converts all error responses to 418 just for the memes, meaning the it may support spaces but HV would assume it doesn’t. A non-reference PDS may return the same status codes but have a broken implementation. It’s a minefield.

+1 for putting community.lexicon.service.describe support in the reference PDS impl, and if that’s not an available course of action, updating com.atproto.server.describeServer for spaces.

We’ll need to think harder before implementing something like community.lexicon.service.describe on the Bluesky PDS distribution as it’d probably become something of an implicit standard at that point.

 In the mean time & to unblock things, how about just adding a spacesAlpha boolean to the com.atproto.server.describeServer output? (I might not even put it in the lexicon)

 One step further could be experimentalFeatures: ["spaces-alpha"]

Considering the Bluesky PDS is in the minority of PDS implementations that don’t implement community.lexicon.service.describe , I’d say the lexicon has already become an implicit standard.

 Adding a spacesAlpha boolean or an experimentalFeatures array to describeServer certainly works but, like you said, anything added to the reference PDS becomes implicit standard. That ends up being the same as implementing community.lexicon.service.describe .

 I’d wager it’s better to take the time to sort the standard solution for this, rather than jam something in. Besides, I don’t know that anything is blocked right now. I’ve got a hacky solution above that’s working, so we can just roll with that until we have a better idea of how to handle it moving forward.

Following up on @bnewbold.net ’s comment over in the community.lexicon.service.describe thread:

 Working group: service self-description 

 This API came up in a separate thread as being a requirement

 I wanted to make sure it was clear that I’m not demanding the implementation of community.lexicon.service.describe . My goal with this conversation was to find a solution that allows services to detect support for functionality.

 If my reading of the com.atproto.server.describeServer lexicon’s description is correct, it seem like an ideal place for this information:

 Describes the server’s account creation requirements and capabilities.

 Which I’m reading as…

 Describes the server’s account creation requirements AND describes the server’s capabilities.

 …but maybe that’s not the intent.

 Adding spacesAlpha to the com.atproto.server.describeServer schema seems like a band-aid solution to a challenge I expect we’ll run into again as we build more functionality that requires coordination across core atproto infrastructure.

 I think a better long-term solution would be to update describeServer to be more generically expandable, allowing servers to define new functionality without requiring an update to the core com.atproto.* lexicons. For example, an additionalFeatures string array could look like this:

 {
 "properties": {
 "inviteCodeRequired": {},
 "additionalFeatures": {
 "type": "array",
 "description": "A list of features supported by this server.",
 "items": { 
 "type": "string",
 "knownValues": [
 "inviteCodes",
 "emailVerification",
 "phoneVerification",
 "blobUploads",
 "spaces",
 "ssoGoogle",
 "ssoGithub",
 "ssoApple",
 "ssoDiscord"
 ]
 }
 }
 }
}

 Example usage:

 { 
 "inviteCodeRequired": true,
 "additionalFeatures": [
 "spaces",
 "ssoGoogle",
 "ssoGithub",
 "ssoApple",
 "ssoDiscord"
 ]
}

 A open string array also makes it easy for servers to advertise functionality not covered by the core spec (e.g. Tranquil PDS could advertise the SSO items I added above, or the Northsky PDS could advertise Stratos functionality).

IRC prefixes new features with draft- as to distinguish them from the fully ratified form which may have breaking changes from the draft implementation. This is done on live networks, and in my opinion works quite well.

@dholms.xyz @bnewbold.net Have y’all thought anymore about this? I’m closing in on releasing HappyView v3 in the next ~2 weeks, and having a reliable way to detect spaces support would be a huge boon.
